ccp.title: CCP
ccp.subtitle: Consistent Character Processus

promptTemplates.a1:
Act as a professional Storyboard Artist. Generate a high-quality 3x3 grid contact sheet,
composed of 9 distinct cinematic frames. This grid must be based precisely on the character
and overall visual style of the provided reference image.
Character Consistency – Top Priority:
- The character in every single panel must look exactly like the character in the
reference image. All physical features, outfit, and appearance must remain identical
across all nine panels.
- Do not alter, reinterpret, or stylize the character in any way. The reference image is
the absolute ground truth.
- Every panel must show the character from a different angle or framing – the goal is to
build a complete 360-degree visual understanding of the character.
Technical Specifications & Labeling:
- The output must be a single image containing a 3-row by 3-column grid.
- Each individual panel must be clearly labeled with a technical alphanumeric identifier
in its top-left corner, ranging from A1 to C3.
- The only variables between panels are the camera angle, framing, and shot size.
Everything else stays consistent.
The 9-Panel Shot List:
Row A (Establishing Spatial Context):
- Panel A1: Extreme Wide Shot (EWS), High-Angle Bird's Eye View.
- Panel A2: Full Shot (FS), Eye-Level Neutral. Full body, head to toe.
- Panel A3: Wide Shot (WS), Dramatic Low-Angle (Worm's Eye).
Row B (Character & Dynamics):
- Panel B1: Medium Shot (MS), Dutch Angle (Canted Frame). Waist up.
- Panel B2: Medium Close-Up (MCU), Eye-Level Portrait. Head and torso.
- Panel B3: Three-Quarter Back Shot. Character viewed from behind and slightly to
one side.
Row C (Intimacy & Detail):
- Panel C1: Close-Up (CU), Low-Angle "Hero" framing. Head from slightly below.
- Panel C2: High-Angle Medium Shot. Looking down onto the character from above
eye-level.
- Panel C3: Extreme Close-Up (ECU) Detail Insert. A macro focus on a key detail of
the outfit, filling the frame.
promptTemplates.a2:
Create a professional character reference sheet. Match the EXACT visual style of the reference (realism level, rendering, texture, color treatment, aesthetic).
IDENTITY LOCK - CRITICAL:
This is the SAME CHARACTER across ALL 7 panels. NOT different people.
- CLONE exact face: bone structure, features, skin, wrinkles, moles
- CLONE exact body: height, build, proportions
- CLONE exact hair: color, style, length, texture, hairline
- CLONE exact costume: every garment, accessory, detail, wear marks
- Age and ethnicity MUST match source exactly
LAYOUT - TWO ROWS:
TOP ROW - 4 FULL-BODY VIEWS (horizontal):
| FRONT | LEFT PROFILE | RIGHT PROFILE | BACK |
- FRONT: Facing camera, relaxed A-pose, arms 30-45° from body
- LEFT PROFILE: Perfect 90° facing left, same A-pose
- RIGHT PROFILE: Perfect 90° facing right, same A-pose
- BACK: Facing away, same A-pose
BOTTOM ROW - 3 PORTRAIT CLOSE-UPS (centered below):
| FRONT PORTRAIT | LEFT PORTRAIT | RIGHT PORTRAIT |
- FRONT PORTRAIT: Head and shoulders, facing camera, neutral expression
- LEFT PORTRAIT: Head and shoulders, 90° profile facing left
- RIGHT PORTRAIT: Head and shoulders, 90° profile facing right
ALIGNMENT REQUIREMENTS:
- Full-body views: heads at identical height, same scale
- Portraits: faces at identical scale, same crop level
- Portraits centered beneath full-body row
- Even spacing between all panels
- Clean panel separation with thin lines
TECHNICAL:
- Neutral plain background (light grey #d5d5d5)
- Consistent lighting across ALL panels (same direction, intensity, softness)
- Natural controlled shadows — detail preservation, no dramatic mood
- Sharp details, crisp edges, print-ready quality
- Accurate anatomy, clear silhouettes
- NO TEXT, NO LABELS
SAME CHARACTER in all 7 panels - perfect identity consistency.
promptTemplates.b:
Act as a Lead Storyboard Artist and Cinematographer for a high-budget film
production. Your task is to generate a comprehensive 9-panel (3x3 grid)
storyboard sequence that visually narrates a dynamic action scene.
CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS & EXECUTION STANDARDS:
AI SCENE ELABORATION: Based on the concise "USER SCENE INPUT"
provided below, you are to autonomously elaborate and craft a detailed, vivid,
and cinematic scene description. This description must define the specific
environment, time of day, weather, lighting, and atmospheric effects necessary
for a high-octane film sequence.
VIDEO-READY REALISM & DETAIL: The output must consist of photo realistic,
ultra-high-detail cinematic still frames. Focus on lifelike textures, professional
lighting, motion blur (where appropriate), and cinematic depth of field. This
grid serves as a direct visual blueprint for AI video generation.
PANEL LABELING: Each individual panel within the 3x3 grid must be clearly
labeled with a technical alphanumeric identifier in its top-left corner, ranging
from A1 to C3.
SUBJECT REFERENCE (Universal Consistency):
Primary ID: Use the Main Hero Image to define the core identity, facial features,
and the primary high-end cinematic aesthetic.
Technical ID: Use the Character Shot Sheet (3x3 Grid 1) as a definitive spatial
reference to maintain absolute visual fidelity from every camera angle.
Meticulously replicate all unique identifiers, costume components, material
properties, and structural details exactly as they appear in the reference
images. Every visual trait of the subject must be mapped directly from the
sources to ensure 1:1 consistency across all 9 panels.
CINEMATIC VARIETY: Ensure a professional flow of shots. Mix Wide Shots
(WS) for scale, Medium Shots (MS) for action, Close-Ups (CU) for focus, and
dynamic angles (POV, Low Angle, or Dutch Angle) for intensity. The 9 frames
must tell a clear, sequential visual story.
USER SCENE INPUT:
promptTemplates.c:
Act as a professional Digital Imaging Technician and Cinematographer. Your
task is to generate a single, ultra-high-resolution cinematic photograph by
isolating a specific frame from the provided 3x3 storyboard grid and rendering
it with absolute visual fidelity.
Instructions:
1. Frame Selection & Composition: Isolate exactly the composition,
camera angle, and framing corresponding to the user-specified panel
code: [INSERT PANEL CODE HERE, e.g., A2] from the provided 3x3
storyboard grid.
2. Visual Consistency Enforcement: The final rendered image must
maintain perfect consistency with both reference images provided:
- Character Reference Image (Physical Attributes Only): Use this
ONLY to maintain the exact character model, facial features, body
proportions, costume design, accessories, hair style, and any
specific physical details of the character.
- Scene Grid Reference (Lighting & Atmosphere): Use the scene
grid image to accurately capture and reproduce the environment,
lighting conditions, atmospheric mood, color palette, time of day,
weather effects, and overall visual tone of the specific scene
being depicted.
3. Lighting & Atmosphere Priority: The lighting direction, quality
(soft/hard), color temperature, contrast ratio, shadows, and atmospheric
effects must be taken exclusively from the scene grid panel being
isolated, NOT from the character reference image. The character
reference serves only to ensure physical consistency of the subject.
4. Final Output Quality: Generate a single, standalone image in ultra-high
resolution (4K cinematic standard). Ensure the final render is photo
realistic and removes any panel labels (e.g., "A1") or grid lines from the
source storyboard.

The character reference serves only to ensure physical consistency of the subject.
4. Final Output Quality: Generate a single, standalone image in ultra-high resolution (4K cinematic standard). Ensure the final render is photo realistic and removes any panel labels (e.g., "A1") or grid lines from the source storyboard.

a2.human: MODE: Human character. Preserve identity, face, body proportions, costume and styling from the reference while keeping realistic human anatomy and clean professional reference-sheet anatomy.

b.puppet: MODE: Puppet / figurine character. Preserve the exact non-human proportions, head size, limb thickness, body shape, material feel, and stylized construction of the reference. Do not normalize the body toward human anatomy.
b.human: MODE: Human character. Preserve identity, face, body proportions, costume and styling from the reference while keeping realistic human anatomy and cinematic body mechanics.

storyboardVariations: fresh coverage: change the camera angles, shot sizes and staging from any previous version while keeping the same scene, character and story beats
alternate pacing: re-order the dramatic beats and vary the rhythm (more close-ups, punch-ins and reaction frames) for a distinctly different edit
new lensing: shift focal lengths, camera height and movement (low angles, dutch tilts, tracking) to reinterpret the same action
different energy: push the mood and lighting in a new direction (harder contrast, new key light direction) while preserving identity and continuity
